conviction_note: Small positive lean. The July H1 guide implies Q2 operating profit of only ¥771m, 40% of Q1's ¥1,929m. In the pre-Expo year that ratio was 96%, and flagship core sales ran +6% to +9% through Jun-Aug, so a modest H1 beat is likely. It is capped below the 30% disclosure threshold, because unlike last year nothing was pre-released. The full-year guide implies H2 operating profit of ¥2.9bn, below even pre-Expo FY2025's ¥3.37bn, while Expo comps end 13 October and September flagship sales ran +20.1%. A full-year raise is therefore a real chance, but this company held its full-year guide at last year's H1. p_up 60 x abs 2.5 gives +0.5. The findings sum to +1.4 because each carries its own upside if the full-year guide is raised; the scaled number sits below that because a hold is about as likely as a raise.

findings.finding: The H1 guide set on 2026-07-10 implies Q2 (Jun-Aug) sales of ¥27,593m (-15.8% y/y) and OP of ¥771m, against Q1 OP of ¥1,929m. In pre-Expo FY2025, Q2 OP was 96% of Q1. The department-store 月次 for Jun/Jul/Aug show total -6.6/-5.5/-6.9%, existing stores -4.9/-4.0/-5.2%, and the Abeno flagship core +9.1/+7.4/+6.2% with footfall up, so H1 operating profit and sales are likely to land above guide. No pre-release was filed this year (last year one came on 2025-09-26 at +30% OP), which caps the H1 beat below the 30% disclosure threshold: estimate OP ¥2.8-3.4bn against ¥2.7bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last year's H1 print (2025-10-10, beat already pre-released on 09-26) moved +1.17% on the estimated-cadence history. The Q1 print with an H1 raise (2026-07-10) moved +4.75%.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody covers the name (no analyst estimates on kabuyoho), so nobody publishes the Q2-implied arithmetic. If the beat were priced, the stock would have re-rated after the Jun-Aug 月次. Instead it is +1.7% over 20 days and flat today at ¥1,886-1,897. Partly priced all the same: the 月次 are public and the company's conservative habit is visible, so this stays small.

findings.finding: The FY guide (OP ¥5,600m) less the H1 guide (¥2,700m) implies H2 OP of ¥2,900m. That is below H2 of FY2026 (¥4,098m) and below pre-Expo H2 of FY2025 (¥3,370m). Yet the September 速報 shows the flagship core +20.1%, a record 大北海道展, and domestic and inbound sales both strong, with total sales down only 5.3% against a peak-Expo comp that ends 13 October. Last year's Nov-Feb base was also hit by the China travel advisory. That makes an FY raise at this print a real possibility.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY guide raised at the Q1 print: +4.75% (2026-07-13). FY guide down at the FY print: -2.8% (2026-04-10). FY held at last year's H1 print: +1.17%. Note the company kept its FY OP at ¥5,400m at H1 last year and delivered ¥6,718m, so a hold is about as likely as a raise.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades at about 19.6x the company's FY EPS of ¥96.6. A market already expecting H2 OP near ¥3.5-4bn would have marked it up after the 1 October September 速報, but the 5-day run-up is only +2.0%. With no coverage, nobody publishes a street number above the company plan, so a raise would be new information.
findings.independence: FY/H1 guide arithmetic from the 2026-07-10 revision (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260710/140120260707588894.pdf), and the company's own cost caveat for H2 (中東情勢 cost inflation, in the same document) cuts against it. The FY2026 results presentation shows the Expo store drove +10.1bn of Abeno sales (https://www.d-kintetsu.co.jp/corporate/ir/upload_file/tdnrelease/8244_20260401597087_P01_.pdf), so the H2 comp genuinely eases after mid-October.

findings.why_not_priced: Margin shorts are a stock of positions that must be bought back, not a flow already in the price. Their effect shows only on a positive surprise. Some of the balance may be 優待 cross positions left over around the August record date, which would make it weaker fuel.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: no pre-release this time (one came last year), so the H1 deviation is probably under 30%; an FY OP raise from ¥5.6bn is possible, roughly a coin flip given the company held at H1 last year. Shareholder returns: year-end-only ¥20 dividend, no interim; no change at last year's H1, so unlikely. New-year guide: not applicable (H1). Quarter: Q1 OP progress was 70.9% of the H1 guide and 34.4% of FY, against 16% and 19% at Q1 in the two prior years, so progress is far ahead of the company's own history.

rejected_candidates.detail: The same series as finding 1. The decline is the Expo-store comp already built into the -15.8% Q2 implied guide, so it is merged there, not filed as a separate negative.

baseline_tension: Agrees with the mildly positive priced lean (+0.07, from the margin overhang) and cuts against nothing in the run-up (+1.7% over 20 days). The strongest negative the release could carry is an FY guide held or trimmed on Middle East cost inflation, as at last year's H1. I looked for it: the company's own July caveat is the only support, and it is why p_up stops at 60.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a series the market already has is priced) is written for negatives; applied by symmetry to the positive H1-beat finding, because the 月次 are public: trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4. p_up was left at 60, so the lesson moves one number once.
Rule 2 (check for a negative tilt) does not bite on a positive call. The strongest negative the release could carry is recorded in baseline_tension.
Open question 3 (a prior 修正 kills the event): no H1 pre-release exists this time; the July revision was made at Q1, so the event stays live. Nothing changed.
